title: Who Gets to Move the Recipe? How Autonomous Agents Earn Decision Authority in the Fab
gist: Guest author Ajay Kumar Govindaram (byline in text; raw author field is 'Admin') argues that fabs already own the best governance framework for agentic AI — tool qualification, SPC, out-of-control action plans and management of change — and should enroll agents as a new kind of operator on a four-rung autonomy ladder granted per decision class. Promotion requires shadow-mode agreement, a minimum sample and stable SPC on the agent's own behavior; demotion is automatic when the agent's control chart signals, and autonomy is capped by tool data observability, which limits brownfield 200mm lines.

insights.claim: Agentic AI pilots in fabs typically stall not because recommendations are wrong but because nobody can say when the agent may act alone, who approved it, and what happens to its privileges if its behavior changes, so fabs keep a human on every action.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Without governance, agent ROI cases that assume unattended decisions never close — governance tooling is the bottleneck, not model accuracy.
insights.quote: Most agentic systems have no answer, because they were built to be smart, not to be governed.
insights.locator: The Question Every Agentic Pilot Skips

insights.claim: An agent kept under human approval for every action becomes an expensive suggestion box, and the business case that assumed some decisions would eventually run unattended never closes.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Vendors selling 'smart' agents without an autonomy path face stalled pilots and churn.
insights.quote: The agent becomes an expensive suggestion box

insights.claim: Gartner predicted (June 2025) that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end-2027 due to escalating costs, unclear business value and inadequate risk controls; the author argues risk control is most of the story in a fab.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Expect high cancellation rates in industrial agent deployments where risk-control is unresolved.

insights.claim: The cost asymmetry in a fab is extreme: an ignored recommendation costs minutes, while an unauthorized recipe change costs every wafer processed before it is caught, so model accuracy alone can never justify autonomy.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Agent adoption in high-cost-of-error manufacturing will be gated by downside control, not upside accuracy.
insights.quote: An unauthorized recipe change costs every wafer that runs before someone catches it

themes.theme: Fab governance as the AI governance template

insights.claim: The semiconductor industry already runs a mature, audited system — tool qualification, statistical process control, out-of-control action plans and management of change — that decides which actor may alter which parameter on what evidence, and it predates agentic AI by forty years.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Fab-native governance know-how could become exportable IP for agent platforms in other regulated industries.
insights.quote: I think the semiconductor industry is sitting on the best framework anyone has for governing agentic AI, and it predates the technology by forty years.

insights.claim: The author reframes the design problem from 'how do we govern AI' to 'how do we enroll a new kind of operator into the governance we already run', treating an agent as a fast, tireless operator subject to the same rules as people.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Agent vendors that integrate with existing MES/quality workflows rather than inventing parallel governance should win fab adoption.
insights.quote: An agent is just a new kind of operator.
insights.locator: An agent is just a new kind

insights.claim: Every agent action and every deliberate choice not to act should be logged with the evidence, the rung the agent was on and what it was allowed to do, so agents appear in the same change-control queue and audit trail as human engineering changes.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Audit-grade logging is a product requirement for fab agents, favoring vendors close to quality systems.
insights.locator: The Record Has to Satisfy Audit

themes.theme: Four-rung autonomy ladder per decision class

insights.claim: The proposed autonomy ladder has four levels: observe (silent conclusions), recommend (engineer acts or ignores), act with approval (human confirms a proposed lot hold or recipe tweak), and act within limits (autonomous execution inside a tightly bounded envelope).
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete maturity model to benchmark fab-agent vendor claims against.
insights.locator: Four Levels, and Nobody Starts at the Top

insights.claim: Authority should be granted per decision class rather than per agent: one agent can be at level four for low-risk, high-frequency nuisance-alarm sorting while staying at level two for setpoint moves on critical layers.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Earliest unattended agent use in fabs will be alarm triage, not recipe control.
insights.quote: Authority is per decision class, not per agent

themes.theme: SPC on the agent: earned promotion, automatic demotion

insights.claim: Promotion up the ladder should require three gates: shadow-mode agreement with engineers above a threshold, a sample large enough to be meaningful, and a stable control chart on the agent's own conduct.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Agent qualification may become a formal, time-consuming step that slows but de-risks deployment.

insights.claim: The key innovation is running SPC on the agent itself — charting its override rate, false-hold rate and size of proposed recipe adjustments over time like any process parameter.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Agent behavior monitoring is a new product category adjacent to fab SPC/yield software.
insights.quote: The move here is to run SPC on the agent.

insights.claim: In the author's prototype shadowing a run-to-run loop, the first warning sign was not a bad recommendation but the agent's override rate drifting upward over about a week, which the control chart caught before the author did by eye.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Behavioral drift precedes visible errors, supporting continuous monitoring over periodic review.
insights.quote: The chart on the agent’s behavior caught the drift before I did.
insights.locator: I’ll admit why this gate won

insights.claim: When any agent behavior metric crosses a control limit or a Western Electric run rule fires, the agent should automatically drop a rung of authority before the next decision executes, without a review meeting.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Interlock-style automatic demotion is what makes autonomous agents deployable in safety-critical settings.
insights.quote: An interlock doesn’t debate; it trips.
insights.locator: This is the fab instinct software

insights.claim: The author contends that automatic, pre-agreed responses to out-of-bounds conditions are the fab instinct software culture lacks and the most valuable thing semiconductor manufacturing can teach agent builders.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Software-native agent platforms may underweight hard interlocks, creating an opening for industrial-grade governance layers.

themes.theme: Observability caps autonomy in brownfield fabs

insights.claim: Running SPC on an agent requires clean, time-aligned tool data, which modern 300mm lines mostly have but older 200mm or mixed brownfield lines often lack, so agents there cannot safely climb past recommending.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Agent autonomy gains will accrue first to 300mm fabs; 200mm/mature-node fabs lag unless they invest in connectivity.
insights.quote: authority is capped by observability, for software exactly as for people

insights.claim: Fabs wanting more autonomous agents now have a concrete ROI reason to finish deferred tool-connectivity and data-quality work.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Second-order demand driver for fab connectivity, equipment-data and data-platform vendors.

themes.theme: Industry moving to trusted data first

insights.claim: PDF Solutions' Exensio Aurora, introduced in September 2026, was built to run agentic AI across manufacturing operations at petabyte scale on a contextualized, trustworthy data layer, which the author reads as confirmation that trusted data must precede autonomy.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: PDF Solutions positioning as the data foundation for fab agents is aligned with this governance thesis.
insights.locator: When PDF Solutions introduced Exensio Aurora

insights.claim: The fabs that win the agentic era will be those that already know how to grant and revoke authority on evidence, not those that buy the smartest agent.
insights.speaker: Ajay Kumar Govindaram
insights.so_what: Competitive advantage shifts to process discipline and data infrastructure rather than model choice.
insights.quote: The fabs that win the agentic era won’t be the ones that bought the smartest agent.
